messages:
alex: anyone else seeing a sudden burst of dropped gRPC streams from inference pods in eastasia GPU farm? started ~04:00 UTC, lots of app-level reconnects

maria: yep. metrics show node conntrack near capacity and pod-level resets. noticed elevated retransmits too.

kevin: @oncall-bot which node is highest right now?

oncall-bot: node-gpu-45 eastasia1-gpufarm nf_conntrack_usage=98% (alert triggered 1945678842)

samir: I ssh'd into node-gpu-45 and ran a quick check:
```
# conntrack -S | egrep "tcp|entries"
entries : 255488
tcp: 200k established, 80k time_wait
udp: 3k
```
Also `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` => 262144

alex: thats fairly close to max. i'm also seeing a lot of SNAT entries that stick around after pod restarts. suspect SNAT port leak from bursty pod churn in prefetch service.

maria: increasing nf_conntrack_max is a quick mitigation but we need the root cause. can you dump iptables nat/conntrack stats?

kevin: ran these on node-gpu-45:
```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
# conntrack -L | grep MASQUERADE | wc -l
42000
# ss -s
TCP:   360k total, 120k established, 80k timewait, ...
```
I bumped nf_conntrack_max to 524288 (`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288`) to give headroom.

samir: why are entries accumulating so long? i see lots of STALE/TIME_WAIT even when pods are gone. also saw this in dmesg that looked like an RDMA/MTU mismatch between hosts and switch: 
```
[  123.456] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: devlink notice: MTU mismatch detected on eth0 (1500) vs ib0 (9000): fragmentation/retransmit observed
```
that causes retransmits and long-lived partial flows.

alex: we do heavy east-west streaming for model prefetch. long-lived TCPs that stall -> lingering conntrack entries + SNAT ports held. combined with aggressive pod restarts for the prefetchers, you get port churn and conntrack exhaustion.

maria: couple mitigation items:
- short-term: keep nf_conntrack_max bump and enable conntrack gc more aggressive (lower tcp timeout for CLOSED/FIN_WAIT)
- mid-term: reduce pod churn on prefetcher (backoff restarts), add local LRU cache on node to reduce east-west chatter
- long-term: audit SNAT strategy (move to egress-gateway or use hostPort for prefetchers)

kevin: suggested sysctl tweaks i applied on node-gpu-45:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=432000
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```
Note: increased established timeout to avoid premature reclaim in case of long-lived streams; lowered FIN timeout to clear TIME_WAIT faster. we should discuss values.

samir: reproduced locally by rapidly restarting ~120 prefetch pods; conntrack fills with STALE entries. list of commands i used to reproduce and mitigate:
```
# reproduce
for i in {1..120}; do kubectl delete pod prefetch-$i --namespace=infra; done
# mitigation
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
conntrack -D -f /tmp/stale-list.txt  # selective cleanup (generated from grep)
```

alex: i've opened a short-lived runbook: reduce prefetcher replica count from 200 -> 140 and hold until we deploy a fix. also tagging model-team to pause aggressive prefetch rollouts.

maria: i'm creating an incident (INC-2026-138) and notifying infra leads. action owners: alex (deploy replica change + runbook), kevin (node sysctl rollout + cluster DaemonSet), samir (repro + write test case), i'll coordinate escalation.

kevin: plan to push a daemonset that proactively bumps nf_conntrack_max on nodes in eastasia and applies tuned TCP timeouts. will also add conntrack metrics to node exporter dashboards.

samir: small note: if we rely on increasing limits we need monitoring alerts for ephemeral port exhaustion too. ephemeral port range currently 32768-60999 on our images. we might expand ephemeral port range on gateways.

alex: TL;DR: conntrack + SNAT port pressure from long-lived, stally east-west model streams + pod churn. mitigations in flight: sysctl bump, scale-down prefetchers, runbook, DaemonSet rollout.

maria: i'll update the incident with timeline and postmortem template. for now tagging :eyes: infra-leads and :thumbsup: from oncall once stable.

kevin: once we stabilize, next steps = evaluate eBPF/LB changes to avoid SNAT for heavy east-west traffic and fix MTU/RDMA mismatch with network team.

alex: thanks all. i will post follow-up when the scale-down is complete and conntrack levels drop. :thumbsup:
